host_state_defect.summary: The stored browser-mode geometry config names a WSL distribution that does not exist on this host, so every command assembled from it fails at the launcher.
measured: wsl.exe -l -v lists exactly one distribution: 'Ubuntu' (Running, WSL2, default)
host_state_defect.discovery_agrees: onshape_geometry_status on the host reports the WSL candidate da4a6b54820703d9b763 with distribution 'Ubuntu', i.e. live discovery knows the right name while the stored config keeps the wrong one.
host_state_defect.impact: Not specific to this feature: onshape_build_geometry_package and every other host-side user of the configured geometry backend fail the same way. browser.ready=true in that status is a CONFIG-level readiness and is not a probe that the command runs.
host_state_defect.sanctioned_repair: onshape_configure_geometry_backend(backend='rest', candidate_id='da4a6b54820703d9b763', confirm_mutation=true) after a dry_run preview. That writes only onshape_rest_api_mode/config/geometry-backend.json (operator state, never touched by an upgrade) and makes this mode's own config the primary for the interference check; the browser config is left alone.
host_state_defect.authority: A production configuration write needs the user's explicit approval, so it was NOT performed in this session. It is the only remaining step between the measured results above and a fully deployed live run.
